facts.text: Lac du Bonnet’s name, meaning "Lake of the Bonnet", was given by French explorer Pierre Gaultier La Vérendrye after the lake’s shape reminded him of a bonnet.
Around 1800, the North West Company built a fur trade post called "Indian Cap Fort" near Lac du Bonnet.
John Duncan McArthur, an experienced railroad contractor and lumberman, worked on the line that reached Lac du Bonnet.
The Lac du Bonnet Mining, Developing and Manufacturing Company, formed in February 1898, brought Winnipeg’s most influential men as executives.
Based at the municipal dock built in 1920‑21, bush pilots opened up the North, cementing Lac du Bonnet’s place in Canada’s aviation history.
The construction of the McArthur Falls generating station raised the Winnipeg River fourteen feet, reshaping Lac du Bonnet’s landscape.
